Road Layer.Specific Description: The roadway had a -2% grade at both the precrash location and point of impact. While a moderate grade, combined with wet conditions, this could contribute to reduced braking effectiveness and increased stopping distances, potentially exacerbating the circumstances leading to the collision.

Infrastructure Layer.Specific Description: The interstate had a concrete divider wall bordering the 3-meter wide left shoulder. While not directly causing the impact, the presence of the wall limited the available space for evasive maneuvers, contributing to the vehicles ending up partially on the shoulder after the collision.

Object Interaction Layer.Specific Description: Vehicle 1 was following Vehicle 2 'too closely' as evidenced by the driver of V2 observing V1 approaching at a âhigh rate of speed and knew he (V1) wouldn't be able to stop in timeâ. This insufficient following distance reduced the time available for V1 to react to the deceleration of V2, directly contributing to the rear-end collision.

There was a 'large longitudinal speed difference' between Vehicle 1 and Vehicle 2. Vehicle 1 was traveling at or near the speed limit while Vehicle 2 was decelerating due to congestion. This differential in speed made a collision more likely when traffic slowed.

Environment Layer.Specific Description: The roadway was 'slippery' due to rainy and wet conditions. This reduced the available friction between the tires and the road surface, increasing the stopping distance required for both vehicles and contributing to the collision.
Adverse weather (rain) was present at the time of the crash. Reduced visibility due to rain likely contributed to the driver of V1 failing to recognize the deceleration of V2 in a timely manner.

Other Relevant Risk Layer.Specific Description: The Ranger (V1) had a left front tire with only 3mm of tread, significantly less than the other tires. This reduced tire grip could have affected braking performance and contributed to the inability to stop in time to avoid the collision.
